SUPERSEDED by F3 (2026-10-28 re-run; same conclusion). Cross-backend fate agr...
nodes.statement: SUPERSEDED by F3 (2026-10-28 re-run; same conclusion). Cross-backend fate agreement is EQUIVALENT to the same-backend baseline within +/-0.05 under a DEPENDENCE-AWARE run-cluster bootstrap (diff -0.0015, 90% CI [-0.003,+0.001]; resampling the 6+6 runs, not the dependent pairs). The margin is not yet biologically justified and the CI is tight mainly because between-run variance is low at this scale. The pair-level p=5.6e-36 is retired as overstated.

nodes.label: SUPERSEDED by F4 (2026-10-28): the 1.00 same-backend baseline was an artifact...
nodes.statement: SUPERSEDED by F4 (2026-10-28): the 1.00 same-backend baseline was an artifact of mechanically deterministic replicates. Exact cell POSITION is NOT backend-equivalent: cross-backend spatial agreement is 1.0 at t0 but 0.08 at the final frame (median drift ~8.5 um), while fate and final areas match. The capstone's "candidate IoU signal" is this representation drift -- the substrate changes where cells sit, not what they become.

nodes.statement: SUPERSEDED by F2 (2026-10-28): the vertex up-gradient climb was produced by the old, uncalibrated linear ActiveMigration mapping. In a mechanics-dominated regime the spatial equivalence TOST REJECTS (cross 0.20 vs same 1.00, diff +0.80 vs margin 0.10), driven by a directed migration difference (vertex A to y~17.9, CPM A to y~10.7). The equivalence test can detect a real substrate difference, so crossparadigm-equivalence's positive verdict is informative, not an insensitivity artifact.
